findings.evidence: Lines 304–307 assume only `SA`, `SB`, `μ`, `μ₁`, `μ₂`, `hincl`, and `hproj`; there is no identification of the `B` terms as duals of the `A` terms or any nondegeneracy/perfectness hypothesis.
findings.fix: Replace “dual” throughout with “compatibly paired” (while retaining dual sequences as an application), and change “anti-self-adjoint” at line 331 to “anti-adjoint.”
findings.issue: The module text, section heading, main-statements list, and line 331 call these “dual short exact sequences” or “anti-self-adjoint,” but the declarations assume only two sequences with compatible pairings; the pairings may even be degenerate, and the two connecting maps act on different coefficient sequences.

summary: The documentation repeatedly describes arbitrary compatibly paired sequences as dual sequences, and one theorem as self-adjoint, although neither duality nor self-pairing is assumed.
